findings.reason: the plan must fix the reader's scope parameter and restate the done-when assertion, or one of the two consumers changes what it measures.
findings.text: §12 does not state the shared reader's scope: read_trees counts only under prefix `reckon` (interface_counts.py:46) while the detector's corpus is `("reckon/", "tests/")` (clones.py:521), so "the detector and the counter see the same path set" holds only if the reader is unprefixed and read_trees filters by prefix afterwards — which the plan never says, and a prefix-scoped reader lifted "as read_trees performs it" would silently drop tests/ from the detector's corpus

findings.reason: the removal check must be scoped to the `if text is not None` line the section actually retires (e.g. `grep -n 'if text is not None'`), not the whole file.
findings.text: the done-when runs `grep -n 'is not None' reckon/interface_counts.py` and requires it to return nothing, but that file carries four other legitimate clauses (:157 AST, :349 view_arg, :466 cache_root, :520 cached), so a literal run of the named check cannot pass and invites deleting `cache_root is not None` at :466, which breaks the cache_root override

findings.reason: the migration must either add a non-raising git variant on velocity (extending the owner) or keep a justified wrapper, and must say whether the corpus cache relocates or keeps its own root.
findings.text: §12 deletes `_git` and `_cache_root` in favour of velocity's, but velocity's `git` (reckon/velocity.py:147) is `subprocess.check_output(..., timeout=180)`, which returns bytes and raises, while clones `_git` (clones.py:644) uses `check=False` and returns a CompletedProcess whose `.returncode`/`.stdout` are inspected by `changed_paths` (clones.py:678) and `_repository_key` (clones.py:425); velocity's `velocity_cache_root` (velocity.py:542) also resolves a different directory (`~/.cache/reckon/velocity`) under `RECKON_VELOCITY_CACHE`, not the detector corpus cache's `~/.cache/reckon/clones` under `RECKON_CLONE_CACHE`, so importing it relocates a cache the plan says "stays"

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new reader on reckon/velocity.py hides the ls-tree listing, the `.py` filter and the one batched `cat-file --batch` read behind a single `(repo, revision, prefix) -> {path: bytes}` call, an interface smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §12 treats velocity's `git` and `velocity_cache_root` as drop-in owners for the detector's `_git` and `_cache_root`, but neither pair is interchangeable, so the substitution breaks callers the plan never names.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §12 states its net explicitly (one public sources reader added on velocity, the public `revised_python` retired, net zero) and §11 states "No definition is added", so each section accounts for its surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §12 proposes one shared source reader but never reconciles the counter's `reckon`-only scope (reckon/interface_counts.py:46) with the detector's `("reckon/", "tests/")` corpus (reckon/clones.py:521), so its "same path set" assertion cannot hold for both consumers; §11's scoped-removal check is an unscoped grep that matches four other clauses.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the reader is not a parallel layer but one home for a composition currently duplicated between read_trees (reckon/interface_counts.py:448-450) and the detector's archive read (reckon/clones.py:659-671); two disjoint consumers justify collapsing them onto velocity.
